title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement - Ninyo & Moore Geotechnical & Environmental Sciences Consultants - Solar Photovoltaic Phase 2 & 3 Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Ninyo & Moore Geotechnical & Environmental Sciences Consultants, Alameda, CA, extending the term of the Agreement (Legislative File No. 25-1220, Enactment No. 25-0861, May 28, 2025) from May 29, 2025, through April 30, 2026 to December 30, 2026, by an additional Two Hundred Forty-Four (244) days, for the latter to provide material testing and inspection services for the Solar Photovoltaic Phase 2 & 3 Project at Horace Mann Elementary School, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Madison Park Academy, Stonehurst Elementary School, and Laurel Child Development Center. The project covers Horace Mann Elementary, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Madison Park Academy, Stonehurst Elementary and Laurel Child Development Center. The original term ran from May 29, 2025 to April 30, 2026, and the amendment adds no money.
vendor_name: Ninyo & Moore Geotechnical & Environmental Sciences Consultants

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Lorena A. Lara - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Lorena A. Lara, Tulare, CA, for the latter to provide interim support for the Nutrition Services Menu Planning and Customized Allergy Responsive Eating Solutions (CARES) Program to ensure continuity of operations doing temporary staffing absence, including, coordinating menu planning activities, reviewing and supporting student meal accommodations, communicating with school sites, nurses, and Nutrition Services staff, maintaining compliance with USDA and California Department of Education regulations, supporting documentation and audit readiness, coordinating with the Central Production Kitchen, troubleshooting operational issues, assisting with weekly planning, providing staff training and guidance on CARES procedures, supporting onboarding and retraining as needed, and ensuring the safe, timely, and consistent delivery of meal accommodations for students with dietary needs; and provide recommendations to strengthen program efficiency, maintain compliance, and support uninterrupted, high-quality nutrition services throughout the duration of the engagement, via Nutrition Services Department, for the period of August 3, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $47,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $47,500 for an interim contractor to support school menu planning and the allergy meal program
summary: An individual contractor will provide temporary support to the Nutrition Services Department during a staffing absence. The work covers menu planning, meal accommodations for students with allergies and other dietary needs (the CARES program), staff training, and keeping up with federal and state food program rules. The contract runs from August 3, 2026 to June 30, 2027, and the board is approving it after that period began.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Central California Advisors - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Central California Advisors, Turlock, CA, for the latter to provide strategic consulting services to OUSD Nutrition Services to support kitchen modernization, equipment procurement, audit readiness, staff training, and improved dining environments; assist with facility and equipment assessments, procurement processes, food safety procedures, kitchen operations, and coordination between the Central Kitchen and school sites, including onsite and remote support, staff guidance, and monthly progress updates to support the District’s transition to fresh, scratch-cooked, and culturally relevant meals, via Nutrition Services Department, for the period of August 26, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $132,000.00.
headline: Hires Central California Advisors for up to $132,000 to help modernize school kitchens and nutrition services
summary: Central California Advisors will consult for OUSD Nutrition Services on kitchen modernization, equipment buying, audit readiness, food safety, staff training and dining spaces. It will also help coordinate the Central Kitchen and school sites as the district moves to fresh, scratch-cooked and culturally relevant meals, with monthly progress updates. The contract runs August 26, 2026 through June 30, 2027, so the service period began before this approval.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Nor-Cal Moving Services - Nutrition Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Nor-Cal Moving Services, Hayward, CA, for the latter to provide general relocation and onsite moving services for the Nutrition Services Department on an as-requested basis during the 2026-2027 school year, supporting the movement of kitchen equipment, furniture, supplies, and related materials between Nutrition Services and OUSD school sites and facilities, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Nutrition Services Department, for the period of September 16, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $20,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $20,000 for Nor-Cal Moving Services to move Nutrition Services equipment in 2026-27
summary: Nor-Cal Moving Services of Hayward will provide moving services for the Nutrition Services Department as needed, moving kitchen equipment, furniture, supplies and related materials between Nutrition Services and OUSD school sites and facilities. The agreement runs from September 16, 2026 through June 30, 2027, for up to $20,000. This is a ratification, meaning the service period began before the Board's vote.

title: Change Order No. 2, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Next Generation of Builders, LLC – Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Renovation Project – Buildings and Grounds Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 2, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Next Generation of Builders, LLC, Santa Clara, CA, for the latter to provide additional work for PCO#10 Hallway Tile Abatement and Drinking Fountain Rework, in the amount of $16,861.84, and PCO#11 Trim/Cleaning Around Windows, Ceiling, and Paint, in the amount of $2881.77, each, as described in the Change Order, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Renovation Project, in the cumulative not-to-exceed amount of $19,742.77, increasing the Agreement price from $250,271.39 to $270,014.16; and extending the term of the Agreement from June 1, 2026, through August 21, 2026  to September 30, 2026, an extension of forty-two (42) calendar days. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $19,742.77 to Next Generation of Builders' Markham Elementary boys restroom renovation contract
summary: This change order pays Next Generation of Builders, LLC for extra work on the boys restroom renovation at Markham Elementary: removing hallway tile that contains hazardous material, redoing a drinking fountain, and trim, cleaning, ceiling and paint work around windows. It raises the contract from $250,271.39 to $270,014.16 and extends the end date from August 21, 2026 to September 30, 2026. The extended work period ended before this October 2026 vote.
source_issue: The two listed change order amounts ($16,861.84 and $2,881.77) add up to $19,743.61, but the text states a cumulative amount of $19,742.77, and the extension from August 21 to September 30, 2026 is 40 days rather than the stated forty-two.

title: Amendment No. 2, Agreement for Inspector of Record Services for Construction - King Construction Inspection, Inc. - Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Room Renovation Project - Department of Building and Grounds
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 2, Agreement for Inspector of Record Services by and between the District and King Construction Inspection, Inc., Oakland, CA., for the latter to provide additional inspection services for the Markham Elementary School Boys Toilet Room Renovation Project, as detailed in the proposal dated September 21, 2026, attached to this Amendment as Exhibit A, in an additional amount of $4,420.00, increasing the not-to-exceed Agreement price from $8,655.00 to $13,075.00.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $4,420 for King Construction Inspection to inspect Markham Elementary boys' restroom renovation
summary: This amendment adds $4,420 so King Construction Inspection, Inc. of Oakland can provide more inspection services for the boys' restroom renovation at Markham Elementary School. The added work is described in a proposal dated September 21, 2026. The contract's maximum rises from $8,655 to $13,075, and all other terms stay the same.

title: Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Data Sync Communication, Inc. – Emerson Elementary School Security Improvement Project - Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 1, Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Data Sync Communication Inc., Berkeley, CA, for latter to cover the remaining balance associated with upgrading the server from a Dell PowerEdge R550 to a Dell PowerEdge R570, as the Dell PowerEdge R550 has been discontinued, as described in the supporting documentation and identified for the  Data Sync Communication Inc - Emerson Elementary School Security Improvement Project, in the not-to-exceed amount of $6,500.00, increasing the Agreement price from $74,000.00 to $80,500.00 and extending the term of the Contract for additional 250 Calendar Days, with completion deadline of September 4, 2026, for the Emerson Elementary School Security Improvement Project. All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $6,500 to Data Sync Communication's Emerson Elementary security project for a replacement server
summary: This change order pays Data Sync Communication the remaining cost of installing a newer Dell server at Emerson Elementary, because the model originally planned was discontinued. The contract rises from $74,000 to $80,500, and the work time is extended by 250 calendar days. The new completion deadline, September 4, 2026, is earlier than this October 28, 2026 meeting.

title: Change Order No. 3, Lease-Leaseback Contract – Cahill Contractors, LLC – Fremont High School Modernization Project – Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Change Order No. 3, Lease-Leaseback Contract by and between the District and Cahill Contractors, LLC, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide additional construction services for the Phase II scope, PCOs 13-17 including the following changes: RFI 59-59.2 Conflicts with Bioretention Wall Elevations at Driveway; RFI 57 Unknown Gas Pipe Near Pile #43; CCD-011A Fire Alarm Changes, Modular Pathway to FACP; Dry-Rot Repairs at Auditorium Bldg. Entrance; and Extended GCs for Auditorium & Project Delays, as identified in PCO’s No.13 thru 17, increasing the Lease-Leaseback Contract amount by $647,761.05, from $11,757,368.71 to $12,405,129.76  and extending the term of the Contract from September 26, 2024 through June 30, 2026 to  August 31, 2026, extending term by 62 calendar days, for the Fremont High School Modernization Project.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $647,761 to Cahill Contractors' Fremont High modernization contract and extends it to Aug. 31, 2026
summary: This change order pays Cahill Contractors for extra construction work in Phase II of the Fremont High School modernization, under a lease-leaseback construction contract. The work covers a wall height conflict at the driveway, an unknown gas pipe, fire alarm changes, dry-rot repairs at the auditorium entrance, and added site management costs from auditorium and project delays. The contract rises from $11,757,368.71 to $12,405,129.76, and the end date moves from June 30, 2026 to Aug. 31, 2026, which is before this vote.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - RDV Consulting Services - Technology Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and RDV Consulting Services, Oakland, CA, for the latter to file the District's E-Rate forms including 470, 471, 472, 486 and 500 to apply for funding and meet E-Rate deadlines to support network services across the District, including the collection of data, providing spreadsheets of collected data, updating school data in EPC and managing PIA reviews and audits, via Technology Services Department, for the period of October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $40,000.00.
headline: Pays RDV Consulting Services up to $40,000 to handle the district's E-Rate network funding applications for 2026-27
summary: RDV Consulting Services will file the district's forms for E-Rate, a federal program that helps pay for school network and internet services, and meet its deadlines. The work includes collecting and organizing data, updating school information in the program's online system, and managing the program's application reviews and audits. The contract runs from October 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027, and the board is approving it after the service period began.

title: Amendment No. 6, General Services Agreement - Terraphase Engineering Inc. - Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 6, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Terraphase Engineering Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide and implement the PEA Work Plan at Garfield Elementary School, including soil-vapor resampling, field investigation and sampling, preparation of the PEA Report, and support through the public comment period and final Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC) approval, as outlined in the Proposal dated August 21, 2026, attached to this Amendment as Exhibit A, for the Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project, in an additional amount of $123,886.00, which includes a contingency fee of $11,262.00, increasing the  Agreement not-to-exceed amount from $163,830.00 to $287,716.00.  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $123,886 to Terraphase Engineering contract for soil-vapor testing at Garfield Elementary
summary: This amendment adds $123,886, including an $11,262 contingency, to Terraphase Engineering's contract. Terraphase will carry out an environmental assessment work plan (called the PEA Work Plan) at Garfield Elementary School for its modernization project. The work includes soil-vapor resampling, field sampling, a written report, and support through public comment and final approval by the state Department of Toxic Substances Control (DTSC). The contract's total limit rises from $163,830 to $287,716.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Cherylynn Moody - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Cherylynn Moody, San Leandro, CA, for the latter to act as a TPA Coordinator for OUSD teachers, facilitating overview sessions for both the general education and special education EdTPA and CalTPA, providing individualized TPA coaching, TPA workshops in December and March, and conducting ongoing case management to ensure that the teachers on the TPA caseload are on track to complete and pass the TPA in a timely manner, via Talent / Human Resources Department, for the period of September 14, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $9,000.00.
headline: Pays a coordinator up to $9,000 to coach OUSD teachers through state teaching performance assessments
summary: An individual contractor from San Leandro will coach OUSD teachers working toward their teaching credentials as they prepare for and pass the required Teaching Performance Assessments (TPA), both general and special education versions. The work includes overview sessions, one-on-one coaching, workshops in December and March, and tracking each teacher's progress. The agreement runs from September 14, 2026 through June 30, 2027, so the work began before the Board's vote to ratify it.

title: Amendment No. 2, Alder GSE Education Services Agreement – Alder Graduate School of Education – Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 2, Alder GSE Education Services Agreement 2027-2028 Extension Amendment (Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - Alder Graduate School of Education), by and between Alder Graduate School of Education and the District, extending the term of the Agreement from September 1, 2024 through June 30, 2027 to June 30, 2028 and authorizing Alder’s Partner Director Contribution (to District) of up to $5,600.00 per enrollee, up to a maximum of 18 residents, for 2027-2028  (Exhibit A-1). title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Men Creating Peace Counseling & Education LLC - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Men Creating Peace Counseling & Education LLC, Olympia, WA, for the latter to provide a total of 127.5 hours of services to support the successful implementation of the Roots of Exploitation Group, with services including providing training, coaching, and ongoing support to group facilitators; developing, reviewing, and refining curriculum content; developing a Train-the-Trainer curriculum and related training resources; and creating and providing supplemental materials, tools, and other support resources needed to facilitate effective and consistent group delivery, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 14, 2026 through November 30, 2026 in an amount not to exceed $12,750.00.
headline: Pays Men Creating Peace up to $12,750 to train and support facilitators of an exploitation-prevention group
summary: Men Creating Peace Counseling & Education will provide 127.5 hours of training, coaching and curriculum work for the Roots of Exploitation Group, a program funded by human trafficking prevention money. The work includes building a train-the-trainer curriculum and making materials so group facilitators can run the program consistently. The contract runs from September 14 to November 30, 2026, and the board is approving it after the work began.
vendor_name: Men Creating Peace Counseling & Education LLC

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Nola Brantley Speaks - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Nola Brantley Speaks, Walnut Creek, CA, for the latter to work with the Human Trafficking Program Grant Manager and related consultants to develop a Survivor Voice Campaign, with the campaign capturing survivors answering questions posed by OUSD youth, with content embedded in postcards, social media, and the program website; identify, hire, and negotiate stipends with survivor participants for the four to eight survivor video features; coordinate with staff who work directly with youth to source the questions youth want to ask; produce one- to two-minute interview clips with survivors for use across the platforms named above, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of September 4, 2026 through December 4, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $5,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $5,000 for Nola Brantley Speaks to produce a human trafficking survivor video campaign
summary: Nola Brantley Speaks will work with the district's Human Trafficking Program to create a Survivor Voice Campaign. The vendor will recruit and pay four to eight survivors and record short video interviews in which they answer questions from OUSD students, for use on postcards, social media and the program website. The work runs from September 4, 2026 to December 4, 2026, and the board is approving it after the work period began.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Michelle Oppen - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Michelle Oppen, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide technical assistance and support to the Center’s Educational Programming, including coaching and support for the Coordinator; preparation and completion of final reports for grants that are sunsetting; review and support for the development and submission of new grant applications; and assistance with annual transition planning to support continuity, sustainability, and effective program implementation, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $11,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $11,000 for a consultant to coach staff and handle grant reports for a student services center
summary: A consultant will give technical help to an unnamed center's educational programs, coach its coordinator, finish final reports for grants that are ending, help with new grant applications, and support yearly transition planning. The work runs October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 through the Community Schools and Student Services Department. This is a ratification, so the board is approving it after the service period began.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - WildCare - Manzanita Community Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and WildCare, San Rafael, CA, for the latter to provide its Wildcare - Wildlife Ambassador Program at an assembly presentation for students on rehabilitated injured wildlife animals and the importance of coexistence with nature at Manzanita Community School, for the period of October 15, 2026 through October 16, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $63.80.
headline: Ratifies $63.80 for WildCare wildlife assembly for students at Manzanita Community School
summary: WildCare, a San Rafael group, presented its Wildlife Ambassador Program at a student assembly at Manzanita Community School about rehabilitated injured wild animals and living alongside nature. The cost is up to $63.80 for October 15–16, 2026. This is a ratification, so the board is approving the agreement after the presentation dates.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Thena Gee Consulting - Early Childhood Development Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Thena Gee Consulting, Sunnyvale, CA, for the latter to design and deliver live professional development sessions and Communities of Practice to support District staff in developing and deepening their understanding and application of mindfulness practices; provide coaching and guidance to OUSD staff who have been trained as mindfulness facilitators to enhance their facilitation skills and sustainability and also deliver facilitator training for a new cohort of participants who have previously completed the EMBRACE training, preparing them to effectively lead and support mindfulness practices within the District, via Early Childhood Development Department, for the period of August 17, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $22,500.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $22,500 for Thena Gee Consulting to train early childhood staff in mindfulness practices
summary: Thena Gee Consulting will run live training sessions and group learning meetings to help district staff use mindfulness practices. It will also coach staff already trained as mindfulness facilitators and train a new group of facilitators who completed the EMBRACE training. The work is for the Early Childhood Development Department from August 17, 2026 through June 30, 2027, and the Board is approving it after the work began.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - WildCare - Esperanza Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and WildCare, San Rafael, CA, for the latter to provide a nature and wildlife presentation for students, giving students an opportunity to be hands-on with animals and learn about taxidermy and skeletons facts as well at Esperanza Elementary School, for the period of September 8, 2026 through May 31, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $561.80.
headline: Ratifies $561.80 for WildCare nature and wildlife presentation at Esperanza Elementary
summary: WildCare, a San Rafael organization, will give students at Esperanza Elementary School a hands-on nature and wildlife presentation with animals, taxidermy and skeletons. The agreement runs from September 8, 2026 through May 31, 2027 and costs up to $561.80. The board is ratifying, or approving after the fact, an agreement whose service period began before this vote.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Elevate Oakland - Academics and Instruction Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Elevate Oakland, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide teaching artist-led vocal music programming through the East Oakland Vocal Program (EOVP), a multi-school initiative serving students across East Oakland at Castlemont High School, Elmhurst United Middle School, and REACH Academy, with potential expansion to Madison Park Academy and Carl B. Munck Elementary School based on school interest, scheduling, and available program capacity, as described in Exhibit A of the Agreement, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, via Academics and Instruction Department, for the period of October 1, 2026 through May 27, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $30,000.00.
headline: Pays Elevate Oakland up to $30,000 for an artist-led vocal music program at East Oakland schools
summary: Elevate Oakland will run the East Oakland Vocal Program, where teaching artists lead vocal music for students at Castlemont High School, Elmhurst United Middle School and REACH Academy. The program may expand to Madison Park Academy and Carl B. Munck Elementary School, depending on school interest, scheduling and available space. The agreement runs from October 1, 2026 through May 27, 2027.
schools: Castlemont High School; Elmhurst United Middle School; REACH Academy

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - BAMA Institute, LLC - Adult and Career Education Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and BAMA Institute, LLC, San Francisco, CA, for the latter to provide accelerated career training for OUSD graduates and current Oakland Adult and Career Education students, by providing a CPR certification course and a didactic instruction phlebotomy course as well as the licensing exam and support, via Adult and Career Education Department, for the period of August 31, 2026 through June 30, 2027, in an amount not to exceed $65,430.00.
headline: Pays BAMA Institute up to $65,430 for CPR and phlebotomy training for graduates and adult education students
summary: BAMA Institute will teach a CPR certification course and a classroom phlebotomy (blood-drawing) course, plus support for the licensing exam, for recent OUSD graduates and current Oakland Adult and Career Education students. The agreement runs from August 31, 2026 through June 30, 2027. This is a ratification, so the service period began before the Board's vote.

title: No-Cost Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Children Rising - Garfield Elementary School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement - 2026-2027 by and between the District and Children Rising, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide weekly individualized literacy and math tutoring for Tier 3 students, who are struggling with foundational literacy skills, often scoring 2+ grade levels below their age group at Garfield Elementary School, for the period of September 14, 2026 through May 31, 2027, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves no-cost Children Rising literacy and math tutoring for struggling students at Garfield Elementary
summary: Children Rising, an Oakland organization, will give weekly one-on-one literacy and math tutoring at Garfield Elementary School. It serves Tier 3 students who are struggling with basic reading skills, often 2 or more grade levels behind. The agreement runs from September 14, 2026 through May 31, 2027, costs the district nothing, and is being approved after the service period began.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Oakland Kids First - Castlemont High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Oakland Kids First, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide supplemental programming at the school focused on increasing student engagement, strengthening positive school culture and climate, and expanding workforce development opportunities, including support for the student leadership class and schoolwide culture and climate activities; implementation of the Cultural Currency Program on campus and operate the Knight Armory, the student store, to provide incentives tied to attendance, positive behavior, and student engagement; have students participate in lunchtime and after-school events, restorative justice circles, attendance challenges, and other activities designed to promote a positive and inclusive school culture; support and/or facilitate school culture events, including the Latino Heritage Assembly, Field Day, Knight Heroes Lunches, and other activities identified in collaboration with school staff; support workforce development; establish an after-school barbering program at the school and continue to facilitate student internships and work-based learning opportunities on the Castlemont Farm and coordinate with school staff throughout the Agreement period to align programming with school priorities, student needs, and the school’s culture, climate, and workforce development goals at Castlemont High School, for the period of August 13, 2026 through September 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for Oakland Kids First school culture and job-skills programs at Castlemont High
summary: Oakland Kids First ran programs at Castlemont High School to boost student engagement, school culture and job skills. The work included supporting the student leadership class, running the student store with rewards for attendance and good behavior, restorative justice circles, school events, an after-school barbering program and internships on the Castlemont Farm. The money had been set aside to hire a part-time (0.40 full-time) site liaison for work-based learning, and will instead fund a part-time (0.30 full-time) Teacher on Special Assignment. The Measures N and H Commission recommended the change, and the total amount does not change.

title: Services Agreement 2026-2027 - Soccer Without Borders - English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2026-2027 by and between the District and Soccer Without Borders, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide year-round after-school and weekend soccer programs, including bi-weekly soccer training sessions and weekly games, for middle school and high school aged boys; school day academic and socio-emotional support, including academic tracking, socio-emotional learning groups, tutoring, mentorship and school reengagement support; and community building trips including team hikes, camping trips, college visits and trips to professional and college soccer games, via English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department, for the period of October 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 in an amount not to exceed $124,440.00.
headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $124,440 for after-school soccer and support for English learner boys
summary: Soccer Without Borders will run year-round after-school and weekend soccer for middle and high school aged boys, with bi-weekly training and weekly games. It will also give school-day academic and social-emotional support, such as tutoring and mentoring, and run trips like hikes, camping and college visits. The work runs through the English Language Learner and Multilingual Achievement Department from October 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027.
